solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make good list for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is chosen for how it sounds when heard

parts.note: a ship that lists or leans over is said to heel

explanation.surface: An instruction to correct a list so that the people checking the accounts are satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants, but here they are simply hearers. To heel is a sailing term for a boat tipping to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal a wound or rift is to repair it, to put matters right again.

clue.text: Design assists in production of cars

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to devise or design it
to back someone is to support or assist them

explanation.surface: Design work helps in the manufacture of cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a type of car with a rear door that opens upwards, so these are models of car.

clue.text: Just like our doctors to get in a state

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the manner of, just like

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the doctors' abbreviation

parts.note: BMA, the British Medical Association, is the professional body of Britain's doctors

explanation.surface: It is typical of British doctors to get worked up into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests agitation, but 'state' is the US state. The BMA is the British doctors' association; A goes after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty United States, in the American Deep South.

clue.text: Girl outside seedy Irish club

indicators.note: the girl's name stands outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: Shelagh is a girl's name, an Irish spelling of Sheila
feeling seedy means feeling unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A young woman stands outside a rundown Irish nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub, but it is a cudgel: a SHILLELAGH is the traditional Irish wooden stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A shillelagh is a stout blackthorn cudgel associated with Ireland, a club used as a weapon.

clue.text: He's fixed up with a modest country dwelling

indicators.note: fixed up as in repaired or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the pronoun gives its letters, the 's being 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A man has been set up with a humble house in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a farmhouse with its land and outbuildings, a rural home.

clue.text: Place that's old, of course, periodically visited

indicators.note: calling at the text at regular intervals picks out every other letter

explanation.surface: A place, which is old of course, that people go to from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of 'old of course'.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a position or site, the particular spot where something happens.

clue.text: Fight through trade winds

parts.note: to trade goods is to exchange them
the wind blows, and blows are gusts of wind

explanation.surface: Battling through the trade winds, as a sailing ship would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade winds' look like one phrase, the steady tropical winds; split them.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange blows is to hit each other, an idiom for getting into a fight.

clue.text: A fool accepting note, one being taken in

indicators.note: the fool takes the note in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a dope is a fool
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fool takes a banknote and is tricked by a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' sounds like being fooled, but it means taken into a family.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoptee is someone adopted, a child received into a new family.

clue.text: Experienced judge's trip of a lifetime?

parts.note: to have had something is to have experienced it
J is the abbreviation for judge, the 's a link

explanation.surface: An experienced judge takes a once-in-a-lifetime journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The hadj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims aim to make at least once, a journey of a lifetime.

clue.text: Beam as delivery arrives on time

parts.note: ransom originally meant deliverance or release from captivity, and still means the price paid for it

explanation.surface: A broadcast beam goes out just as a delivery turns up on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: RANSOM in its old sense of delivery from captivity follows T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar or lintel, a structural beam over a door or window.

clue.text: It's unusual way to extend, and count, old measure

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to range is to extend over an area
to tot up is to count
an ell was an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: An odd way to stretch out a length and count in an obsolete unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase strange to tell introduces something surprising, saying the fact is remarkable.

clue.text: Bats briefly at Lord's, overly trusting partner?

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: to be bats is to be crazy, cuckoo
Ld is the written abbreviation of Lord, as in a title

explanation.surface: A batsman at Lord's, the London cricket ground, is cut short, with a partner too trusting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, which steers you to cricket; here it is only the written title, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckold is a husband whose wife is unfaithful, a spouse too trusting to notice the betrayal.

clue.text: Rarely at rest, in haste avoiding warm-up?

indicators.note: rarely is read as 'in a rare or unusual way', so these letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: Someone seldom resting, and in a hurry, skips the warm-up before exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm-up' suggests stretching before sport; read literally it is getting hot, which a heat-resistant material avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heat-resistant withstands high temperatures without being affected, so it never really gets hot.

clue.text: Giving little ground eg on run with Sue

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so these letters are broken down and remade

explanation.surface: Someone yielding little ground in a dispute, perhaps pressing on with a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like territory being conceded; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ungenerous means being mean or stingy, offering very little to others.

clue.text: A leading poet's with expedition

definitions.note: the answer is a poetic or archaic word meaning with speed or full force

parts.note: the leading thing is the main one

explanation.surface: A leading poet is setting out on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but it means speed; 'poet's' marks the word as literary.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an archaic, chiefly poetic adverb meaning at full speed or with great haste.

clue.text: Reliable English clergyman suspected of murder, somewhat taken aback

indicators.note: only part of the clergyman's title, his abbreviated rank, is turned back to front

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for a reverend, a clergyman
Reverend Green is one of the murder suspects in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US)

explanation.surface: A dependable English vicar has been suspected of murder, which leaves people shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverend Green is the clergyman among the Cluedo suspects; his title shortened to REV is turned back to VER, giving E + VER + GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen performer or song lasts and stays dependable, so the word is used for something reliably enduring.

clue.text: Features in some crustaceans and indeed in European rabbits

indicators.note: the agreement word goes inside the combination that follows

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length
yes, indeed, used as emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: Body parts found in crustaceans, and indeed in rabbits in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on, in British slang, is to chatter at length, which is why rabbits means talks here.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs and lobsters have eyes mounted on movable stalks, so eyestalks are parts of their bodies.

clue.text: Crisis point returning as liquid in well includes fuel

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the next piece within them
returning means these joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, can mean 'as' in 'such as'
ink is the liquid kept in an inkwell
to feed a fire is to fuel it

explanation.surface: A crisis comes as water returns to a well that has fuel in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' suggests a water well, but it is an inkwell; 'as' gives the abbreviation for 'for example', as in 'such as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a knife-edge is being in a precarious, critical state where things could go either way.

clue.text: Cockney person who suggests one's acting?

indicators.note: London Cockney speech drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: a hinter is someone who hints, suggesting
I'm is 'I am', one is I and 's is is

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks who it is that implies someone is only pretending.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners whose accent drops initial H, so HINTER loses its H; 'one's' read as 'I is' gives IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means temporary or provisional, as in an acting manager standing in for now.

clue.text: Undercarriage that is stuck on swamp

indicators.note: the second piece is attached to the end of the first

parts.note: a bog is a swamp or marsh
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A vehicle's undercarriage has got stuck in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogie is the wheeled truck under a railway carriage, part of the running gear underneath.

clue.text: Information masters are inclined to shine

indicators.note: to master something is to get on top of it and hold it, so the outer piece contains the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
ships list when they lean, so things that list are inclined

explanation.surface: Those who master information are inclined to excel.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to gleam or sparkle with reflected light, to shine.

clue.text: PC their primary rank?

parts.note: PC looks like a police constable, the lowest police rank, but read as politically correct thinking it is what Orwell's enforcers of approved thought care about most

explanation.walkthrough: PC means police constable in Britain, the basic rank; the other reading is politically correct, and these police in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four deal in approved thinking rather than ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's dystopian novel the Thought Police punish citizens for unorthodox ideas, making correct thinking their chief business.

clue.text: Tiny binder supposedly at first getting lost under old notepaper

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A small binder supposedly gets mislaid beneath old notepaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binder' looks like stationery among the notepaper; it is a particle physics term.
explanation.definitionFit: A gluon is a subatomic particle thought to bind quarks together, the carrier of the strong force.

clue.text: Risk when fungi is pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ceps are edible mushrooms, porcini

explanation.surface: There is danger when wild mushrooms are picked from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: On spec means as a speculation, taking a chance, so spec is a gamble or venture.

clue.text: Upstart's mean? Not the end of the world

parts.note: par is the average or mean level

indicators.note: the last letter of the planet's name is dropped

parts.note: Venus is a world, a planet

explanation.surface: An upstart is asking whether something mean is not the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World' is the planet VENUS, losing its last letter; 'Upstart's' reads as 'upstart is', so the definition is the upstart itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a social climber who has newly gained wealth or position, an upstart.

clue.text: The state of the loos outrageous!

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wild and out of order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at how filthy the toilets are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the condition of the toilets, but it is a country; loos are toilets in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is an independent southern African kingdom, a sovereign country entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Turn out policies with singular appeal

parts.note: to turn out for an event is to come to it
a party line is a policy, so lines are policies
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Produce policies that have a single, distinctive attraction for voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Comeliness is attractiveness of appearance, the quality of being pleasing to look at.

clue.text: African runners, the latest to be picked up

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio or by ear, meaning the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the latest is the news, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

explanation.surface: Sprinters from Africa, the latest ones, are about to be collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but these are animals; the G in the answer is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are African antelopes that migrate in huge herds across the plains.
